sentences.text: Listracanthus species are chiefly recognized from enormous feather-like denticles that can reach up to four inches in length.
Each denticle bears a prominent central spine surrounded by secondary spines that radiate outward, giving the structure a feather or comb appearance.
Because only these denticles are commonly preserved, the overall body shape of Listracanthus sharks remains largely unknown.
Artist Ray Troll imagines Listracanthus as a gigantic, fiercely bristled frill-shark-like creature with an eel-like body.
Listracanthus shaoyangensis was described as a new species by Fang and colleagues.
The type specimens come from the Longtan Formation in China.
Listracanthus shaoyangensis is regarded as a valid species.
The genus Listracanthus was established by Newberry and Worthen in 1870.
It is placed within the order Eugeneodontiformes and the family Edestidae.
Listracanthus shaoyangensis dates to the Permian Wuchiapingian age.
The genus Listracanthus spans a fossil range from the Late Carboniferous to the Early Triassic.
